thesis: AppLovin Corporation (APP) operates an AI-powered advertising platform that connects advertisers with mobile app publishers and, increasingly, connected-TV inventory. **[Fact]** The company reports two segments: **Advertising** (AppDiscovery user acquisition, MAX in-app bidding, Adjust analytics, Wurl CTV) and **Apps** (a portfolio of 200+ free-to-play mobile games). **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$5.48 billion** (+70% year over year), net income **$3.43 billion** (63% net margin), and free cash flow **$3.97 billion**. **[Fact]** Q1 2026 revenue was **$1.84 billion** (+59% YoY) with **$1.3 billion** of free cash flow. The core economic engine is AXON, an AI recommendation system that matches advertiser demand with publisher supply in real-time auctions at microsecond speed.
why_market_wrong: The market may be treating AppLovin as a cyclical mobile-gaming ad vendor when the business has pivoted toward a durable, high-margin software platform. **[Fact]** Advertising revenue was **68%** of FY2024 total and grew **91%** in segment Adjusted EBITDA that year, while Apps was **32%** and management is conducting a **strategic review** of the Apps portfolio. **[Inference]** Generalists anchoring on 2022 losses or gaming cyclicality may underweight the AXON data flywheel: more advertiser spend improves models, which improves return on spend, which attracts more spend. There is no dated catalyst; the inefficiency is **descriptive** (complex ad-tech story, dual-class control, privacy-regulation overhang) rather than a timed equity yield curve setup.
